title: Ho Chi Minh City street AI cameras identify a masked burglar by gait, build, clothing and face; Tân Hưng ward police detain him within two days
summary: HCMC street AI cameras identified a masked burglar who took two laptops and 14 million VND on 23 December 2025; police held him on 24 Dec.
account: Early on 23 December 2025 an intruder entered a rented room at 62 Street 51, Tân Hưng ward, Ho Chi Minh City. He took two laptops and the wallet, identity papers and bank card of the tenant, H.A.T., 33. From his account, 14 million VND was withdrawn. He reported it that morning. Tân Hưng Ward Police and the Criminal Police Division used the street AI camera system. It analyzed the masked man's gait, build, clothing, movement and facial data, identified him and reconstructed his route. At 11 p.m. on 24 December officers found Phạm Ngọc Huy, 23, of Ninh Bình, at an internet café on Tô Ký street. He was a convicted thief. He confessed. Property recovery is not reported.
purpose: Ho Chi Minh City's street AI cameras are run by the police for security and investigation. VnExpress describes the technology analyzing and matching biometric features. Identifying a suspect from footage is the use the police describe. The system and its vendor are not named.
system: Ho Chi Minh City police street AI camera system (unnamed): facial recognition with gait, body-shape, clothing and movement analysis
deployer: Ho Chi Minh City Police (Tân Hưng Ward Police with the Criminal Police Division, PC02)
segment: Public-space surveillance with facial and gait recognition

ratings.reason: H.A.T. had the intruder who took his laptops, papers and 14 million VND identified, detained and confessing within two days. No source reports recovery of the property or the money. So the benefit to him is resolution, not restitution.
Tân Hưng Ward Police and PC02 cleared a masked-intruder burglary in under 72 hours. Seven outlets carried the case as the police's demonstration of the AI camera system.

ai_role.statement: The system's contribution was identification. It matched the masked intruder's gait, body shape, clothing, movement and facial data and reconstructed his route. That pointed police to him. The detention, confession and case-building were police work. The system and its vendor are not named. No official is quoted by name. Every report draws on the police account. The OECD Monitor tags the entry under privacy and data governance and respect of human rights, the concerns that come with public facial recognition.

produced_by: Street AI cameras covering the route the intruder took, with footage retained for police review.
A model that matches people on gait, body shape, clothing and movement as well as face, so a mask does not defeat identification.
A prompt police report, the morning of the burglary, and a ward investigation team able to act on the match within hours.
must_hold: The suspect passes through camera coverage and can be found at a fixed location afterwards, here an internet café.
Identification is confirmed by police work and a confession. The sources report no independent check of the match.
The system and vendor are unnamed, so performance beyond this case cannot be checked.

headline: HCMC AI cameras identify a masked burglar; police detain him

later.note: The 25 December 2025 reports end with the suspect's confession and the ward police consolidating the file; no prosecution or trial report was found.

revisions.change: Record drafted from the OECD Monitor entry and five Vietnamese reports of 25 December 2025. Benefit created or restored as the classifier proposed: a post-hoc investigation that resolved a burglary, not a prevented harm. The detention time differs between outlets: Tuổi Trẻ gives 23h on 24–12, Công an nhân dân the night of 24 to 25 December, VnExpress and VietNamNet date the arrest 25 December, and Thanh Niên prints “23 giờ ngày 25.12”, which postdates its own 11:52 publication and is treated as a misprint; the date observed is 24 December. The Monitor's Pháp Luật TP.HCM link resolved only to a headline stub and is not cited; the Công an nhân dân link redirected from cand.com.vn to cand.vn when read. The victim's year of birth is 1992 (VietNamNet, CAND); the suspect's is 2002. Property recovery is not mentioned in any source; the suspect is reported to have sold the items.
Benefit type set to Reduced Violence under Trustible's full taxonomy of 23 types; it was Improved Organizational Efficiency among the six first used.
Country of the deployer added from the organization's own site or a registry.
Prose pass: a rating reason, account, purpose, the replication conditions, the system's part rewritten in shorter sentences with abbreviations expanded; facts, figures and quotations unchanged.

fields.account: Early on 23 December 2025 an intruder entered a rented room at 62 Street 51, Tân Hưng ward, Ho Chi Minh City. He took two laptops and the wallet, identity papers and bank card of the tenant, H.A.T., 33. From his account, 14 million VND was withdrawn. He reported it that morning. Tân Hưng Ward Police and the Criminal Police Division used the street AI camera system. It analyzed the masked man's gait, build, clothing, movement and facial data, identified him and reconstructed his route. At 11 p.m. on 24 December officers found Phạm Ngọc Huy, 23, of Ninh Bình, at an internet café on Tô Ký street. He was a convicted thief. He confessed. Property recovery is not reported.

revisions.change: Record drafted from the OECD Monitor entry and five Vietnamese reports of 25 December 2025. Benefit created or restored as the classifier proposed: a post-hoc investigation that resolved a burglary, not a prevented harm. The detention time differs between outlets: Tuổi Trẻ gives 23h on 24–12, Công an nhân dân the night of 24 to 25 December, VnExpress and VietNamNet date the arrest 25 December, and Thanh Niên prints “23 giờ ngày 25.12”, which postdates its own 11:52 publication and is treated as a misprint; the date observed is 24 December. The Monitor's Pháp Luật TP.HCM link resolved only to a headline stub and is not cited; the Công an nhân dân link redirected from cand.com.vn to cand.vn when read. Country of the deployer added from the organization's own site or a registry.

fields.summary: HCMC street AI cameras identified a masked burglar who took two laptops and 14 million VND on 23 December 2025; police held him on 24 Dec.
fields.account: Early on 23 December 2025 an intruder entered a rented room at 62 Street 51, Tân Hưng ward, Ho Chi Minh City. He took two laptops and the wallet, identity papers and bank card of the tenant, H.A.T., 33. From his account, 14 million VND was withdrawn. He reported it that morning. Tân Hưng Ward Police and the Criminal Police Division used the street AI camera system. It analyzed the masked man's gait, build, clothing, movement and facial data, identified him and reconstructed his route. At 11 p.m. on 24 December officers found Phạm Ngọc Huy, 23, of Ninh Bình, at an internet café on Tô Ký street. He was a convicted thief. He confessed. Property recovery is not reported.
